# dsh-plugin-mesh

> DSH Mesh is a plugin for DeepSeek Harness (dsh) that discovers other dsh instances on the local network over UDP multicast or port scan, shows each peer's self-reported capabilities in a sidebar panel, and dispatches tasks between machines in both directions — over the LAN, or over an automatically downloaded userspace Tailscale (tsnet) sidecar when machines are not on the same network.

Canonical package: `dsh-plugin-mesh` (npm, MIT).
Repository: https://github.com/peng456/dsh-plugin-mesh
Showcase: https://peng456.github.io/dsh-plugin-mesh/
Primary documentation language is Chinese; this file is the English, machine-oriented entry point.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-mesh                 # 'desktop' profile: must run in DSH Desktop's own terminal
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-mesh   # any other profile: a normal terminal is fine
```

From source instead: `git clone https://github.com/peng456/dsh-plugin-mesh && cd dsh-plugin-mesh && ./install.sh`

`dsh plugin --profile desktop ...` is rejected from a normal terminal by dsh itself (bin.js:29 — the desktop profile is managed exclusively by the Electron application). Use the app's built-in terminal, or `install.sh`.

**A restart of the dsh host is required after install** — the plugin loads at startup.

Verify after restart: `GET http://127.0.0.1:45917/mesh/v1/health` returns JSON containing `{"app":"dsh-mesh","machine":"<name>",...}`.

## What it does at runtime

- Sends a JSON heartbeat to UDP multicast `239.255.42.99:45892` every `announceIntervalMs` (default 5000 ms) and listens on the same group.
- Reports a structured `osInfo` card entry (host) and a `systems[]` array: host first, then environments such as WSL distros on Windows (`kind: "wsl"`, Linux `platform`, distro name/version). Fields per system: `platform` (`win32`/`darwin`/`linux`/`android`), `name`, `version`, `distro` (Linux), `kernel`, `desktop` (Linux), `arch`. Older peers only send `os`; the UI falls back to parsing it. Purely display data, no auth impact; at most 4 systems are transmitted.
- Serves a small HTTP peer API on TCP 45917 (configurable via `port`).
- Optionally starts a bundled Go sidecar running a userspace Tailscale node (tsnet). No TUN device is created, so the host cannot route to `100.x.y.z`; all tailnet traffic is proxied through the sidecar. The binary is downloaded per-platform on first use and verified against checksums pinned in the plugin source.
- Auto-creates an agent session on the receiving machine when a task arrives, then routes that task to a new or reused session.

## Tools registered (callable by the agent)

| Tool | Parameters | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `mesh_peers` | `includeOffline?: boolean` | List discovered peers: online state, address, OS, user, and the capabilities each peer reports. |
| `mesh_scan` | none | Actively scan the local subnet for mesh peers. Use when multicast is blocked. |
| `mesh_run` | `peer: string` (required), `task: string` (required), `thread?: string`, `noWake?: boolean`, `newSession?: boolean`, `workspace?: string` | Dispatch a task to another machine. Asynchronous — a successful call means "accepted", not "done". |
| `mesh_tasks` | none | Show recently received and sent mesh tasks. |

`peer` accepts a machine name, an instance id, or `ip:port`. **Do not pass `machine/user`** — `from` fields look like `machine/user`, but the peer key is the machine name only.

Reuse the same `thread` value for the same piece of work: the receiving side reuses one session per `thread`, which saves tokens and keeps context. Use `noWake: true` for pure acknowledgements — otherwise a task wakes an agent session on the peer.

`newSession: true` forces a fresh session while keeping the same conversation key (i.e. it is still the same conversation, with a clean context).

## Configuration

Override by id in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: mesh
  config:
    requirePairing: true
```

**`config:` is replaced wholesale, not merged** (dsh's patch layer does `target[key] = value`). To add one key you must restate the keys you want to keep, or the others fall back to schema defaults.

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | |
| `machineName` | string | `""` | Human-readable name; empty = ask/derive from hostname |
| `port` | natural | `45917` | HTTP peer port |
| `announceIntervalMs` | natural | `5000` | Multicast heartbeat period |
| `peerTtlMs` | natural | `20000` | Peer marked offline after this silence |
| `requestTimeoutMs` | natural | `20000` | Per-request timeout |
| `useMulticast` | boolean | `true` | |
| `scanOnStart` | boolean | `true` | |
| `scanIntervalMs` | natural | `60000` | |
| `scanConcurrency` | natural | `64` | |
| `scanTimeoutMs` | natural | `800` | |
| `pingIntervalMs` | natural | `10000` | LAN health probe period |
| `tsnetProbeIntervalMs` | natural | `60000` | Tailnet health probe period |
| `requirePairing` | boolean | `false` | **Default off: the peer API accepts unauthenticated task POSTs.** Setting it `true` here pins pairing on; otherwise the Mesh panel's pairing switch (persisted in `state.json`) decides |
| `agentPreset` | string | `"standard"` | Agent preset for auto-created sessions |
| `permissionPreset` | string | `"workspace-write"` | Permission preset for auto-created sessions |
| `workspaceRoot` | string | `""` | |
| `tsnetEnabled` | boolean | `false` | |
| `tsnetAuthKey` | string | `""` | Tailscale auth key; must be reusable |
| `tsnetControlUrl` | string | `""` | |
| `tsnetHostname` | string | `""` | The plugin prefixes `dsh-`; do not include it yourself |
| `tsnetPermissionPreset` | string | `""` | Empty = same as `permissionPreset` |
| `maxWakesPerThread` | natural | `30` | Per-thread wake cap per window |
| `threadWindowMs` | natural | `3600000` | Window for the cap above |
| `threadCooldownMs` | natural | `5000` | Cooldown between session-creating wakes |
| `minTaskChars` | natural | `24` | Bodies shorter than this are not woken (inbox only) |

## Tailnet setup (the only step that needs an external account)

Cross-network links require a free Tailscale account and an auth key. Create one at
<https://console.tailscale.com/admin/settings/keys> — that URL redirects to sign-up
if you are not signed in yet. The key **must be Reusable**; single-use keys fail
with `invalid key` on the next start. If device approval is enabled in the tailnet,
tick Pre-approved as well.

Set `tsnetEnabled: true` plus `tsnetAuthKey` in config, or paste the key once into the
Mesh panel's tailnet card — it is stored in `~/.dsh/mesh/state.json` (mode 0600) and
never needs re-entry. The plugin's UI links to the key page directly; do not tell users
to hunt for it.

## Network and security facts

- Ports: TCP `45917` (peer HTTP), UDP `45892` (multicast group `239.255.42.99`).
- Discovery is intentionally public: any host on the same L2 network can see the machine and its self-reported card.
- With `requirePairing: false` (the default), **any host that can reach TCP 45917 can POST a task, which wakes an agent session** using `permissionPreset`. Turn on the pairing switch in the Mesh panel (immediate, no restart) or set `requirePairing: true`, and make both machines share one secret, on untrusted networks. The token travels in a plain HTTP header — it guards against stray devices, not against a network sniffer.
- The shared secret is stored in `~/.dsh/mesh/state.json` (mode 0600) alongside `machineName`, the persisted `instanceIds`, and the tsnet auth key. It is never included in the multicast card.
- Persistent identity is a UUID per profile; the OS machine fingerprint is used only to reclaim a reinstalled device (same name, or the old record already offline). Two live instances on one physical machine are kept separate.
- Sidecar binaries are verified against sha256 checksums pinned in `lib/tsnet/checksums.js` — deliberately not fetched from the same release, so a hostile mirror cannot swap both.

## Requirements

- A dsh host that can load cordis plugins with a client half (DSH Desktop, or `dsh web` + a profile).
- Node >= 20 for development. Peer `@deepseek-ai/*` packages are provided by the host and are not bundled.
- No Go toolchain and no Tailscale client are required by end users.

## Development

```bash
npm run check            # version consistency + TDZ scan + syntax + loadability
npm test                 # = check + four regression suites (~138 assertions, network-free)
npm run selftest:caps    # capability collection: sanitising, GPU parsing, retries, claim rules
npm run selftest:client  # client bundle rendering without a browser
npm run selftest:prompt  # task prompt generation
npm run build:sidecar    # rebuild the Go tsnet sidecar (cross-platform)
```

`AGENTS.md` in the repository root carries the operating guide for coding agents: hard constraints, known traps, and file map. Read it before changing this project.

## Documentation map

- `docs/index.html` — user-facing showcase, Chinese (GitHub Pages)
